explanation: This is safe. The `if (!p) return;` guard means the dereference on the following line only executes when p is non-null, so a NULL pointer can never be written through and no null-pointer crash is possible. A tempting wrong answer reads the dereference and concludes it crashes when p is null, missing the guard directly above it.
prompt: set() may be called with a null pointer. Does *p = v ever crash?
